drafts.title: Front seats: longer thigh support and reliable memory restore
drafts.description: Front seats must provide noticeably longer thigh support for tall drivers and reliably restore drivers' saved positions so drivers feel supported and do not need to re-adjust after each use.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion extends forward by at least 40 mm versus the current model measured at the cushion leading edge; seat memory restores saved seating position within ±10 mm (linear) and ±1° (angular) and completes the restore action within 3 seconds in ≥95% of 100 automated cycles.
assumptions: Mechanisms and software allow an additional 40 mm usable cushion extension without reducing other adjustment ranges
±10 mm / ±1° tolerance is perceived by customers as 'correct' seat restore based on internal UX benchmarks
uncertainties: Variation in occupant body shapes may require different optimal extension for perceived comfort
Exact measurement method for 'cushion leading edge' must be finalized with interior engineering

drafts.title: Rear legroom at least equal to main competitors
drafts.description: Rear-seat occupants must have legroom that matches the segment's main competitors so rear passengers no longer feel cramped compared to rival cars.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear knee room (hip point to forward surface of front seatback) ≥ 930 mm when front seats are adjusted to a representative driving position; measured in vehicle prototypes and at least equal to the competitor average in our target set.
assumptions: Competitor average knee room for this segment is approximately 930 mm based on market benchmarking available at design start
Measurement uses a consistent fixture and occupant reference points (to be defined in test plan)
uncertainties: Actual competitor knee-room numbers may change; final target can be adjusted within program constraints

drafts.title: Convenience features work reliably for daily use
drafts.description: Everyday convenience features must accommodate common items and work reliably so customers can use the car without repeated attempts or workarounds.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept bottles up to 75 mm base diameter and a 1 L tumbler and retain them under 0.5 g lateral acceleration in ≥95% of tests; hands-free tailgate opens on the first standard foot gesture within 2 seconds in ≥95% of 50-user trials; ambient lighting offers at least 64 selectable colors and 5 distinct brightness steps accessible from the user profile menu; a 12 V trunk socket provides continuous power sufficient for a 40 L cooler (up to 120 W) and is reachable for typical cooler placement; exterior door handles operate and open within 5 seconds after ice exposure and at −25 °C in ≥95% of cycles.
assumptions: Standardized test methods exist or will be defined for cup-holder retention and tailgate gesture testing
Trunk 12 V socket continuous power of 120 W is sufficient for typical portable coolers customers want to run
Ice exposure test method will simulate realistic roadside freezing conditions
uncertainties: Actual cooler power draw varies; this requirement does not guarantee run-time beyond vehicle battery/alternator constraints
Different user foot gestures may require user education or calibration

drafts.title: Side windows and cabin noise feel solid and quieter at highway speeds
drafts.description: Side glazing should give customers a feeling of solidity and reduce cabin noise so highway travel feels more refined.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Exterior-to-cabin noise level at 100 km/h is reduced by at least 2 dB(A) compared with the current model when measured with identical road/tire conditions (per the program test method).
assumptions: A 2 dB(A) reduction is perceptible and valued by customers as 'quieter' in this segment
Test comparisons use the current model as baseline on the same test track and tires
uncertainties: Noise benefits depend on other vehicle systems (tires, seals, body stiffness); glazing alone may not achieve full reduction

drafts.title: Physical volume control with precise, repeatable adjustment
drafts.description: The physical volume control must allow customers to change audio level precisely and quickly without looking at a screen, giving a predictable tactile experience.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Users can change volume in ≤1 dB perceived steps using the physical control and successfully tune to a target level without looking in ≥95% of attempts within 3 seconds (measured across 30 test users).
assumptions: Perceived 1 dB step is realistic and sufficient for users; audio system supports 1 dB adjustment increments
User test consists of representative ambient cabin noise for tuning tasks
uncertainties: Some users may prefer finer or coarser granularity; accessibility needs may differ

drafts.title: Pedestrian protection compliance (customer request — regulatory scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the front end meet the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for product feature definition; tracked as a regulatory compliance item.
drafts.scope_reason: Request is specifically about meeting regulation/homologation requirements rather than a customer-experience feature.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification (customer request — regulatory scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the rear seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for feature drafting; tracked as a certification/regulatory item.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a regulatory/certification request and not a direct customer-experience specification.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern follows ECE R112 where applicable (customer request — regulatory scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that headlights follow the ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for product feature drafting; tracked as a regional homologation requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: This signal requests conformity to specific lighting regulations; compliance belongs in homologation workstreams, not product-experience requirements.

drafts.title: Explicit engineering spec: 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (engineering specification — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customer requested that the volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder (specific component-level requirement).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specification only — not handled as a customer-facing requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a request for a specific component/part (engineering specification) rather than a customer-experience requirement.

drafts.title: Explicit engineering spec: 4.5 mm laminated side glass (engineering specification — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customer requested 4.5 mm thick laminated side windows (specific glazing thickness).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specification only — not handled as a customer-facing requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a specific material/thickness request (engineering detail), so it is logged as out-of-scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Explicit engineering spec: seat cushion foam density 55 kg/m³ (engineering specification — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customer requested that the seat cushion use foam with density of 55 kg/m³ (specific material property).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering specification only — documented for engineering evaluation.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a request for a specific material property (engineering specification) and therefore out of scope for customer-facing requirement definition.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (out of scope for product requirements)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60 percent after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for product feature drafts; business/financial guarantee topic to be handled by commercial/finance teams.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a commercial/financial request (residual value guarantee), not a vehicle feature specification.

drafts.title: Production cost reduction request (out of scope for product requirements)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW cut production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for customer-facing product requirements; tracked as a program-level target for manufacturing/finance.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a production/cost target, which belongs to manufacturing and program management rather than a customer-experience requirement.
